title: Data Entry Registration
intro: A message offers a simple data-entry job at home. You only need to pay a small registration fee.
Tap anything that looks odd to sniff it closer. Pin what is suspicious, clear what is harmless.
When you are sure, decide what to do.

screen.context: You are looking for work you can do from home.

pay.label: Big pay for typing
pay.why: Pay far above the work is the bait.

noexp.label: No experience needed
noexp.why: A job with no requirements is not a job.

fee.label: A registration fee
fee.lens: You must pay ₹1,200 to get a login.
fee.why: Honest employers never charge to register.

link.label: A payment link
link.lens: It goes to a payment page.
link.why: Never pay through a link from a text.

refund.label: "100% refundable"
refund.lens: A promise to win your trust.

job.label: A data entry job
job.why: The kind of job is normal. How it hires is not.

actions.label: Search the firm's name with "scam" and look for a real company page
Report the number and delete it

trap.title: EasyWork · Register
trap.ask: Pay ₹1,200 by card to get your login.

block_report.line: Reported and deleted. Your phone company can block the number.

verify.line: A search showed many warnings, and the firm had no real company page. Case cracked.

ignore.line: You stayed safe. But the same scam is still landing on other people.

go_ahead.line: The ₹1,200 went to a stranger. No login came, and more "fees" followed.

what_if.go_ahead: Honest employers never charge to register. A search for the name would have shown the warnings.
what_if.ignore: Reporting takes two taps and helps protect other people.
what_if.verify: Checking was smart. Reporting it as well helps protect other people.

golden_rule: A job that charges you to register is a scam. Real employers pay you, not the other way round.

quick_check.q: A data-entry job asks for a ₹1,200 registration fee, refundable after a month. What do you do?

options.text: Do not pay. Search the name with "scam", and report the message

quick_check.explain: Honest employers never charge. A refund promise is bait.

hints.nudge: Who pays whom in a real job?
